guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul “Old Black” / Martin D-45
guitar.evidence: Neil Young's 1953 Gibson Les Paul "Old Black" and his Martin D-45 acoustic are both extremely well documented signature instruments.

tone.target: warm acoustic-electric clean with subtle chorus and room
tone.profile: warm acoustic-electric clean with subtle chorus and room
tone.summary: A gentle signal chain emphasizing warmth and clarity: Compression -> Clean Boost (optional) -> Chorus -> US Deluxe Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab, finished with Room reverb for subtle ambience.
corrections: make it more acoustic than electric

rig.name: Neil Young - Harvest Moon - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Gentle compression to smooth dynamics and add sustain, mimicking fingerpicking warmth.
Optional gentle boost for added presence on chords (kept inactive to maintain subtlety).
blocks.gap: The Boost module is generally used for grit; keeping it off ensures maximum cleanliness.

blocks.purpose: Adding the required subtle chorus effect for a shimmering, 'acoustic-electric' feel.
Bypassed to ensure pure clean tone and avoid any crunch or distortion.
Selecting a classic, warm, clean Fender-style tone suitable for acoustic emulation.
Providing a bright, articulate cabinet sound that complements the clean US Deluxe amp model.
Subtly shaping the tone to enhance warmth and roundness, compensating for potential brightness.
Adding the required subtle ambience without sounding like heavy echo or reverb.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default US 2x12 IR for a more natural, warm acoustic tone.

proposals.reason: The current bright cab may sound too electric; needs warmth to match the 'Harvest Moon' feel.
